correctness.rationale: Write q=(e_x-e_y)/sqrt(2) and v=(gamma(e_x+e_y)+sum_z w_z e_z)/sqrt(2). For every real diagonal F, [D,F]q=(f(x)-f(y))v, so ||[D,F]|| is at least sqrt(C) times the gap. For the gap-one potential supported on {x,y} with values +1/2 and -1/2 the entire commutator is vq^T-qv^T. It vanishes off span(q,v), and its two nonzero singular values when C>0 are both ||v||=sqrt(C). Scaling attains the bound. For C=0 both rows have no off-diagonal entries, and the same potential can be scaled arbitrarily. D's diagonal commutes with every F and does not enter. Substitution gamma=0 or 1 and sum w_z^2=k gives both unweighted cases and their ratio. Independent symbolic spot check: python3 -B /workspace/reproduce_frozen.py 2 verifies the two witness identities with arbitrary symbolic weights, diagonals on the pair, outside edge and potentials on a four-point space; the argument above proves all sizes.

evidence: Besnard identifies the same distance on the union of simple paths from x to y. Iochum–Krajewski–Martinetti compute complete and complete-minus-one-edge cases by explicit commutator norms. Clare et al. describe the general edge-removal question and solve the path problem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Pruning can retain arbitrary outside edges—for example an edge between two common neighbors lies on a simple x-to-y path. It does not force the sharp local expression. Neither paths nor the uniformly weighted complete model accounts for variable signed weights or arbitrary outside blocks.

evidence: For uniform edge weight a, Proposition 5 states |a|^(-1)sqrt(2/n) and |a|^(-1)sqrt(2/(n-2)) before and after removing the distinguished edge. Thus the deletion factor is known for complete graphs. The other exact overlaps concern zero pair coupling and unit external weights.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The retained generalization is not a change in normalization: weighted pair and outside profiles now vary independently and one has exact independence from the outside graph even where pruning does not simplify it. There is no general edge-deletion claim.

evidence: Clare et al. use the same commutator distance for graph adjacency but the inspected explicit general-family formulas concern paths.

The triangular-graph record uses automorphism averaging and antisymmetry for adjacent pairs, not externally identical rows; the odd Boolean hypercube record uses coordinate symmetries for antipodes, whose outside profiles differ for odd dimension at least three.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The exact equivalent symmetry is the transposition of the two vertices after ignoring the diagonal of D, not symmetry of the rest of the graph. Indeed replacing f by (f-f composed with the transposition)/2 preserves its gap and does not increase the norm. This is the standard reason the variational problem reduces to a one-dimensional signed potential, but the graph-specific statements located do not present the resulting general closed formula.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These match false twins with respectively q, p, and 2r-2 external common neighbors. They are exact overlap, not independent evidence for universal weighted coverage; the publication day alone does not order the records.

originality.rationale: Exact complete-graph/deleted-link formulas and two same-day false-twin specializations are established coverage. The supported distinction is the sharp common-profile formula for arbitrary real weights (either zero or nonzero pair coupling), independent of the whole outside submatrix. The located sources and related records do not cover that statement. Antisymmetrization is a standard symmetry argument, not itself a new method here.

An equivalent result under point-swap symmetry in earlier finite spectral geometry remains possible; no absolute priority asserted.

value.rationale: The substantive result is exact ambient-independence for a natural class of vertex pairs, not the elementary averaging trick or the known complete-graph value. For a graph joined to two twin apices it determines their distance without solving the surrounding distance problem and gives an exact edge-deletion response independent of every internal edge of the base. It also covers signed weighted attachments, and provides a sharp norm certificate and optimizer.
